integrity.authorization: caller-asserted: ok means consistent and attested under the trust anchor given here; it authorizes a change only when that anchor (and --base) is supplied by the host from the hosting service's protected branch, in a check the change under review cannot edit

limits: A passing gate says the history is approved, the claims and the model agree where VCV can check them, and every required criterion's mapped test cases passed in a run captured here. It does not say those tests check the right thing: a mapping is an agent's or a person's claim.
Agent observations are interpretations. VCV checks that the objects, files, lines and test cases they cite exist; it never confirms or refutes what they say.
Tests were run by the host's own runner, outside VCV. A run is host-observed only when this process captured its report; how far that report can be trusted is how far the job that produced it can be.
